name: EPR evidence and closed-loop record keeper
demand: The regulatory need is genuine but narrowly scoped: eligible waste must be household food-grade plastic, collected by or for the producer, kept unmixed, sent to one accredited reprocessor or exporter, and recycled into food-grade material. Producers must supply that operator’s evidence and validate its figures: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/extended-producer-responsibility-for-packaging-closed-loop-recycling. The 2026 producer register is downloadable and was updated 22 October 2026, but its page does not state an aggregate count or identify closed-loop registrants: https://report-packaging-data.defra.gov.uk/public-register. An Environment Agency report says there were 344 UK packaging direct registrants in the 2025 compliance year; that is not the total producer population or the eligible closed-loop market: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/packaging-producer-responsibility-monitoring-plan-2025/compliance-monitoring-and-enforcement-activity-2025. Search volume, installs, users, number of closed-loop participants, and product demand are unverified.
prices: A broad pEPR reporting product lists £25, £50, and £90 monthly plans, or £250, £500, and £900 yearly: https://peprcompliance.co.uk/pricing.php. PackTotal quotes an initial implementation cost and annual licence without publishing prices: https://www.packtotal.co.uk/packaging-data-management-software/pricing/. The statutory closed-loop registration fee is £2,548 per year; it is paid to the regulator, not a software vendor: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/extended-producer-responsibility-for-packaging-closed-loop-recycling. These are advertised prices and a regulatory fee, not proof of software sales or willingness to pay.

revenue_proof.claim: No dated paid-revenue event for a directly comparable closed-loop evidence ledger was verified. The cited competitor page publishes prices, not completed sales.

copy_speed: Adjacent product launches show fast-moving competition: The Packaging Portal reported Valpak’s Global Data Insights platform launch on 16 April 2026, covering packaging, supplier data, EPR costs, and reporting: https://www.thepackagingportal.com/industry-news/valpak-launches-global-epr-platform/. Lappa’s newsletter dated 22 September 2026 says its Shopify-to-EPR integration is in pilot: https://lappa.org/blog/newsletter/newsletter-september-2026/. Normantics advertises UK EPR evidence-linked records and document extraction but says it is in development; its launch date is unverified: https://normantics.com/. I found no dated launch confirmation for an exact producer-to-accredited-reprocessor closed-loop ledger.
platform_risk: High. PackUK’s central digital service handles producer registration, data submission, automated validation, and fee calculations, and its 2026–27 plan says the service will continue developing: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/packuk-operational-plan/packuk-operational-plan-2026-to-2027. Closed-loop data must ultimately be reported through the government service, which specifies CSV fields and rejects invalid rows: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/extended-producer-responsibility-for-packaging-closed-loop-recycling. Compliance schemes can register members for closed-loop reporting, creating an existing alternative to a standalone product: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/extended-producer-responsibility-for-packaging-closed-loop-recycling.
defensible_asset: There is no moat in the proposed concept alone. Government producer and accredited-operator registers are public and downloadable: https://report-packaging-data.defra.gov.uk/public-register and https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/public-register-of-reprocessors-and-exporters-of-uk-packaging-waste. A potential asset would be permissioned, longitudinal links between producers, packaging lots, operator evidence, accreditation status, and validation history. Reprocessors and exporters must retain audit records for 7 years, supporting the value of reliable evidence history, but this does not establish a producer-side switching cost: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/packaging-waste-regulatory-requirements-and-compliance-for-reprocessors-and-exporters.
build_effort: Moderate for a prototype; production effort is unverified. The government reporting format provides a bounded CSV workflow, while the evidence rules require linking documents to eligibility conditions and validating operator figures: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/extended-producer-responsibility-for-packaging-closed-loop-recycling. A useful product would need document intake and extraction, product or lot matching, accredited-operator checks, evidence provenance, exception handling, and CSV export. AI could extract fields and flag gaps; the required validation process and regulatory responsibility make automatic approval risky. No public integration feed or API for reprocessor evidence was verified.
channel: Use a branded site with an evidence-readiness checklist, search-led content, and opt-in webinars or referrals through packaging associations, compliance schemes, and consultants; this need not depend on Ricardo’s personal brand. For direct B2B email, limit outreach to verified corporate subscribers such as limited companies or LLPs, identify the sender, provide a valid opt-out, and handle named contact data under UK GDPR. ICO guidance says sole traders and some partnerships are individual subscribers and require consent or a valid soft opt-in for unsolicited email or text; social DMs count as electronic mail: https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/.
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified. The <=5 hours/week constraint is not demonstrated; support for missing or disputed third-party evidence, onboarding, and rule changes could require recurring manual work. Pilot with real evidence packs before relying on this limit: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/extended-producer-responsibility-for-packaging-closed-loop-recycling.
desk_test: One-day desk test, not run: download the current producer and accredited-reprocessor registers; identify producers with public evidence of food-grade plastic collection or tray-to-tray recycling; make a static mockup of evidence upload, eligibility checks, and report export; then ask for a paid pilot or evidence pack through opt-in channels or compliant outreach to verified corporate subscribers. Exclude sole traders and individual subscribers from unsolicited electronic outreach. Register sources: https://report-packaging-data.defra.gov.uk/public-register and https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/public-register-of-reprocessors-and-exporters-of-uk-packaging-waste. Outreach rules: https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/.
red_flags: The main trigger has passed: the 1 October 2026 deadline to register for 2027 closed-loop data and the 1 October deadline for January–June 2026 data are both past as of 23 October 2026: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/extended-producer-responsibility-for-packaging-closed-loop-recycling. The eligible segment is much narrower than the general packaging EPR population; opted-in producer count, software revenue, demand, and the ability to stay under 5 owner-hours/week are unverified. The idea looks more defensible as a focused workflow feature or partner tool than as a standalone business until a producer or reprocessor commits to a paid pilot.
